Story 07 — OpenAPI contract checked against the served routes (Story: CRM-22)

## Prerequisites

- **Sprint branch exists.
** `sprint-0` is already cut from `main` (created by the first sprint-0 story, per lesson **L-3** in `.
squad/plan-lessons.md` lines 29–36 and the

branch model in `docs/git.md` lines 12–19). Cut the story branch as `CRM-22-openapi-contract` from `sprint-0` and merge back into `sprint-0`.
- **PLATFORM
-6-API (CRM-21)** completed: `api/src/app.js` mounts a single `express.Router()` at `/api/v1` with `healthRouter()` at
`/health`, and `platform/http/errors.js` owns the `DOCUMENTED` catalogue (see `api/src/platform/http/errors.js` lines 15–24).

This story extends the existing chain, it does not restructure it.
- **Coordination with feature authors.** Every subsequent `-API` story
(e.g. PLATFORM-8-API / CRM-23, IDENTITY-1-API / CRM-41) adds its route and its `paths` entry in the same commit; the check this story install

s is what forces that simultaneity. No feature route is added here.

---

## Story Goal

Give the API a machine-checkable cont

ract:

1. A hand-authored `api/openapi.json` document that names every route the running app serves and which of the eight statuses in

`DOCUMENTED` each route may answer.
2. A router-walker that reads the actual `express.Router` stack of a freshly built `createApp()` and returns the set of served `(method, path)` p
airs, using a single **exported prefix constant** as its input (the mount path is not recoverable from Express

5's layer — see intake).
3. A test that fails **and names the offending route** when the served set and

the documented set diverge in either direction.
4. A live route `GET /api/v1/openapi.json` that returns the document, so a client can fetch the contract from the running

application. This route documents itself.
5. A small `api/requests.json` request collection that a smoke test replays against `app.listen(0)`; each request must res

olve to a status other than 404 or 500.

Not in scope: request/response body schemas, feature routes, seed data (PLATFORM-8-API /

CRM-23), a rendered documentation UI, and authentication on the document route.

---

## Context — Read These Files First

1. `.squad/plan-lessons.md` — read wh
ole file. Pay particular attention to **L-11** (lines 141–153): every status the document names must be one of the eight in `DOCUMENT
ED`; and **L-12** (lines 155–167): a plan that touches the mount seam lists every test file that reaches through it.

Also **L-10** (lines 123–139): the walker replaces, and must not sit next to, a hand-rolled text scan.
2
. `.squad/stories/platform/CRM-22/intake.md` — read whole file, especially the "Technical hints" block (lines 130

–184) and the "Out of scope" block (lines 186–201). The Express 5 layer notes there are authoritative for this repo.
3. `scripts/criteria/platform.

md` **lines 81–93** — the four acceptance criteria this story owns.
4. `api/src/app.js` — read whole file (58 lines). The composition root; `create
App(deps = {})` builds the chain, `const v1 = express.Router()` at line 44 is mounted at `'/api/v1'` at line 51. The pr

efix literal at line 51 and the mount-path comment at lines 41–43 are what this story turns into a constant.
5. `api/src/platform/http/health.js` —

read whole file (14 lines). `healthRouter()` registers `GET /health` on a sub-router; this is the one currently served route.
6. `api/src/platform/http/errors.js` **lines 15–24** —
`DOCUMENTED` (frozen map of the eight statuses: 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 429, 500). Every `responses` key in `openapi.json` must be

one of these numbers as a string (L-11).
7. `api/src/app.test.js` — read whole file (190 lines). It uses `deps.mountTestRo
utes` to attach throwing / echoing routes for tests; the walker in this story must run on `createApp()` with **no deps** so those test

8. `api/src/platform/http/request-id.test.js`, `api/src/platform/http/request-logger.test.js`, `api/src/platform/http/security-headers.test.js` — gr
ep them for `mountTestRoutes` and `/api/v1`. All three reach through the same seam. If the prefix constant introduced in this story is
ever moved later, **every** file that imports it or spells `/api/v1` must move with it (L-12). This story does not move the mount; it

only names it.
9. `api/package.json` — dependencies list. **Do not add any dependency**: Express 5.2.1 is already install
ed; the test runner is `node --test` (line 12); Node ≥ 22.13 is guaranteed (line 7) so

`fetch` and `import.meta.dirname` are available.
10. `docs/git.md` **lines 12–19** — branch model: cut `CRM-22-openapi-contract` from

`sprint-0`, merge back into `sprint-0`, delete the story branch.

, before you introduce the constant.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **A route is added without a do
c entry.** The contract test computes `served − documented` from the two sorted sets and asserts the difference is empty; when it is not, the

failure message names each offending `METHOD /path`. Enforced in `openapi-contract.test.js` (task 6 below).
- **A doc entry no

longer has a serving route.** Symmetric check: `documented − served`; also named per entry. Same test file.
- **A response status outside `DOCUMENTED`.** The contract
test iterates every operation's `responses` and asserts each key is either a `2xx` string or a stringified status in `DOCUMENTED` (values im
ported from `errors.js`). Guard for **L-11** — the plan does not add a source-scan check, because the constructor in `errors.js` (

lines 32–34) already refuses undocumented `HttpError`.
- **A test-only route registered through `deps.mountTestRoutes` leaks into the served set.** The walker in
the contract test runs on `createApp()` with **no** deps; the seam is only reached when `typeof deps.mountTestRoutes === 'function'` (`app.js` line 48

), so the served set is exactly the production tree.
- **Prefix / walker disagreement.** A dedicated assertion in `route-table.
test.js` asserts `collectRoutes(createApp(), API_V1_PREFIX)` includes `'GET /api/v1/health'`. If either the prefix constant or the walker drifts, this test names the drift by

failing on the missing element rather than a count.
- **`openapi.json` is malformed.** `openapi.js` calls `JSON.parse` at module load;
a broken document throws immediately when `createApp()` is imported, and every test in `api/src/` go

es red. This is the desired failure mode — a silently 500-ing document is worse.
- **`openapi.json` moves.
** `openapi.js` resolves the path relative to its own `import.meta.url` (via `fileURLToPath`) so a file move that keeps the rel

ative layout still works, and a move that breaks the layout fails loudly at module load with a clear `ENOENT`.
- **A path with multiple HTTP methods.** The

walker emits one entry per method; the document lists methods as separate keys under the same path. The sorted set compares cleanly.
- **A
request in `requests.json` resolves to 404 or 500.** The replay test asserts `status !== 404 && status < 500` and names the failing request by

its `name`. This is what the fourth acceptance criterion requires.
- **No dependency added.** Verify by grepping `api/package.json` after implementation

— the `dependencies` block must still be `{ "express": "^5.2.1" }` (see current content, line 15).

---
